answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and ships walnut crates to eight counterparties. Each crate bears a violet-ink seal, serial bound to the sender key. At dawn the ledger snapshots counterparty sets; auditors check seals, and a self-trading ring loses its bonds. First 34, kth 34+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. One crate cannot serve two recipients; reuse burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 34 once, keeping its bond.
